correctness.rationale: The separable-collapse proof is valid directly from the ultrapower quotient. For each n, separability gives a countable \(2^{-n}\)-ball cover of the bounded range; countable completeness forces one inverse image into the ultrafilter. The corresponding centers form a Cauchy sequence, and every bounded family is equivalent to its constant ultralimit. For X=ell_1, standard fresh-coordinate witnesses prove octahedrality, while \(x=(2^{-n})_{n\ge1}\) has no single unit y with both ||x+y||_1=2 and ||-x+y||_1=2 because equality forces y coordinatewise both nonnegative and nonpositive. Thus the countably complete ultrapower is isometric to ell_1 and is not rigid octahedral.
risks: Existence of a free countably complete ultrafilter is a large-cardinal-dependent hypothesis; no existence claim is made.
